concern: Novelty claims extended beyond the selected accessible corpus.
correction: Bound claims to the reviewed studies and identify the preprint as closest located work, without asserting worldwide absence.

concern: The proposed comparison was called pre-registered without evidence of a completed registration.
correction: State that protocol and analysis will be frozen before final runs; keep the document prospective.

concern: The stated search window extended through December 2026, beyond the October submission.
correction: Close eligibility at 20 October 2026.

concern: Full-text accessibility and database coverage could bias conclusions about gaps.
correction: Describe this as a focused accessible-corpus review and explicitly limit the inference.

concern: Ranking edition, category and verification status were not consistently explicit for the new journals.
correction: Use 2025 JCR / 2024 JIF consistently; verify Sensors Q2 (II), Electronics Q2 (EE) and Q3 (CS-IS), Scientific Reports Q1 (MS) against the archived official table; add the actual source citation.

concern: The WeiDetect auxiliary-size claim pointed to Table 9 rather than the CSE-CIC-IDS2018 Appendix Table 11; its scope and the reported +70% magnitude were easy to overread.
correction: Correct the table, name the auxiliary-pool denominator and dataset-specific setting, and remove the ambiguous percentage/percentage-point magnitude.

concern: Score gaps, uncertain samples, rare-class confusion and acquisition triggers were treated as stronger causal evidence than they provide.
correction: Distinguish demonstrated results from plausible vulnerabilities and hypotheses; label-poisoned features need not be outliers.

concern: Missing repeated-seed uncertainty was sometimes equated with proof that no repeated runs occurred.
correction: Retain the documented single seed in P11; qualify P12/P13 as lacking reported repeated-seed uncertainty.

concern: Fixed 3/8/12/15 output widths did not explain what happens when rare classes lose training support.
correction: Treat these as maximum widths, omit classes with no usable training rows, and freeze actual widths/eligibility before final runs.

concern: Aligning MachineLearningCSV feature rows to separate metadata rows was not identifiable in the presence of duplicates.
correction: Project numeric features and metadata from the same TrafficLabelling row; use MachineLearningCSV as the schema reference; prohibit positional/value-only joins.

concern: Session identity, endpoint direction and reconstruction uncertainty were underdefined.
correction: Use unordered endpoint-and-port pairs plus protocol and interval-based 120-second idle gaps, with data-only threshold sensitivity and a metadata feasibility gate.

concern: Session isolation and exact-content isolation could conflict if split assignment was done separately by class.
correction: Group connected components of session and duplicate links before assigning splits/owners; quarantine conflicting labels and retain deterministic same-label survivors.

concern: Per-family chronology could be mistaken for globally future-only testing, especially with mixed-label components.
correction: Use one fixed group-stratified split with approximate ratios and explicitly limit conclusions to simulated class arrival; report dates and host/testbed confounding.

concern: T0, later benign cohorts, scaler behaviour and metadata availability needed coherent boundaries.
correction: Use isolated Monday T0 only for the frozen scaler, forbid refitting/clipping and fresh-record reuse; permit IDs for bookkeeping but exclude metadata from predictive inputs.

concern: Row counts alone did not define adequate group support or guarantee nonempty acquisition sets.
correction: Add a distinct-component floor, required anchors/source and at least one eligible untargeted new family in each acquisition stage; call the floor operational rather than a power guarantee.

concern: The external dataset was budgeted without an explicit transferred source-family/schedule protocol.
correction: Make it conditional on an independently locked schema, source mapping, schedule, dose and isolation audit; transfer method settings only.

concern: The equal-client 10% global corruption example did not describe the actual Dirichlet ownership design.
correction: Report realised global and source-local denominators, admitted poison and aggregation weights.

concern: Dose draws were not explicitly nested or protected from filter-induced changes to random-number consumption.
correction: Use nested prefixes of one eligible-ID permutation, common attack IDs across arms, and separate random streams.

location: Threat model; pilots; budget; failure taxonomy
concern: Fallbacks changed attacker count/maximum dose while the final four-dose grid and contrasts remained underspecified.
correction: Keep one attacker and the original four doses for confirmation; report weak/null attacks and require a separate exploratory protocol for stronger threats.

concern: Hyperparameter pair values, pilot defaults, score aggregation and tie-breaking were missing.
correction: Specify the grids/defaults, one common synchronisation budget, clean development tuning, and deterministic ties; reuse DR settings for its admission variants.

concern: An identical E1 checkpoint was not fully specified as model plus persistent client state.
correction: Clone replay, counters and random states as well as weights; retain all final seeds regardless of attack effect.

concern: Loss ranking of new classes depended on newly initialised outputs, stochastic scoring and undefined ties.
correction: Expand before scoring, disable dropout, freeze one scorer per stage, break ties by immutable ID, and acknowledge that novelty scores may be unreliable.

concern: It was unclear whether counts/new-class protection could access true labels or poison markers.
correction: Register supplied current labels before filtering and use only supplied labels for counts/quotas; restrict reference labels to the builder/evaluator and oracle diagnostic.

concern: Admission could be read as applying to memory only, while all current rows still trained.
correction: Use admitted mini-batches and admitted IDs for both training and replay insertion; bypass memory in FT/EI.

concern: Zero-current-data clients and repeated-epoch/replay counts were not explicitly excluded from aggregation weights.
correction: Weight distinct admitted current rows once, exclude inactive clients, and invalidate a stage with no active clients.

concern: The anchor, importance owner, evaluation point and relation to the final aggregate were incomplete.
correction: Broadcast the final shared model, update client-local importance there once, anchor at that model, preserve old importance and zero-pad new coordinates.

concern: The design could be mistaken for exact Fisher-EWC and canonical DER++ implementations.
correction: Identify squared minibatch-mean gradients as an approximation and explicitly disclose masked/normalised, post-update-logit DER++-style choices.

concern: First-pass insertion was ambiguous across multiple synchronisation rounds, and reservoir fairness did not name the admitted population.
correction: Persist seen-ID/counter state across rounds/epochs, consider each admitted ID once, and specify replay sample size and the empty-memory case.

concern: Storage timing, dropout state, head alignment and post-broadcast refresh were undefined.
correction: Cache post-update evaluation-mode logits once, align by class ID, and leave stored logits unchanged across broadcasts.

concern: Averaging Hulk together with honest new families entangled the adaptation endpoint with the targeted attack endpoint.
correction: Define confirmatory acquisition over eligible untargeted new families; keep an all-new score including Hulk descriptive.

concern: Honest-new admission could be presented as evidence for DC even though it retains those supplied labels by construction.
correction: Treat 100% retention as a mechanism check and require measured untargeted-family F1 for adaptation.

concern: A later source error alone does not establish replay causation or recovery after honest source data return.
correction: Use matched clean trajectories, call H attack-associated persistence, and distinguish withdrawal without fresh source data from recovery.

concern: Replacing poison with unspecified honest records altered several memory fields and did not define a unique causal contrast; the diagnosed arm was unclear.
correction: Use two DC clones per seed; correct stored poisoned labels only, holding IDs/features/logits/weights/states fixed; restrict interpretation to erroneous-label replay and keep 24 continuations.

concern: Undefined precision with no predicted positives could lead to dropping a valid zero-recall/zero-F1 class.
correction: Calculate F1 directly from TP/FP/FN, preserve legitimate zeros, and reserve N/A for actual zero denominators with declared handling.

concern: ACC, BWT, forgetting, test-bank composition and clean FAR timing were named without full operational definitions.
correction: Define stage cohorts, current-head predictions, cumulative scoring, equal-stage ACC, BWT/forgetting and E4 clean FAR on a fixed benign bank.

concern: A generic clean-subtraction formula obscured that H and recall change were already clean-adjusted.
correction: Write their learner contrast as a direct difference. The original is numerically equivalent if its zero-dose adjusted endpoint is correctly set to zero.

concern: Separate C1/C2 error control was legitimate only for the separately scoped question groups.
correction: Strengthen the proposal to one 29-test Holm family for document-wide claims; explicitly note this is a conservative design refinement, not proof the old two-family arithmetic was invalid.

concern: Exact testing and interval language did not fully state symmetry, zero/tie handling or coverage limitations.
correction: Specify sign enumeration on ranked nonzero differences, all-zero p=1, tied ranks, rank-biserial effects and descriptive bootstrap intervals; remove an underqualified exact-interval claim.

concern: P-value resolution could be confused with power, and null significance with robustness/equivalence.
correction: Recalculate the 29-test first-Holm resolution (11 nonzero pairs), state no demonstrated power guarantee, and retain uncertainty/null findings.

concern: Discard-and-fix language did not ensure that all affected matched runs were rerun.
correction: Version repairs, rerun complete matched sets, avoid imputation, and preserve the fixed multiplicity count with unavailable tests reported explicitly.

concern: The original 633-run sum was correct, but clone arms, eight changed settings, cached prefixes and the core/development distinction needed clarity.
correction: Retain 633 full trajectories plus 24 continuations; explain 81 development, 240 core final, and the eight ablation settings.

concern: Raw parameter bytes and a small MLP did not establish total state size or CPU feasibility.
correction: Separate the 76,348-byte raw payload from replay/importance/optimiser/serialisation costs; require pilot timings and report component costs.

concern: Fine-tuning was called a lower bound, which need not hold under poisoning or even clean learning.
correction: Describe it as a reference without explicit retention, which can outperform continual-learning methods; distinguish the low-loss control from actual Co-teaching.

concern: Figure labels implied generic leakage-free data and did not match the corrected acquisition endpoint.
correction: Use group/content checks and honest-new F1; preserve the separate exploratory branch and compact its footer without shrinking diagram text.

concern: A floating glossary interrupted prose; comparison tables crowded one landscape page; section/float barriers produced a nearly empty page; heading/column text overflowed.
correction: Keep tables/algorithms near their introductions, give comparison tables separate landscape pages at 9 pt, fix column widths and wrapping, group the RQs, and fit both diagrams together; add PDF metadata and caption hierarchy.
